_arch_note: exp_g_0033 (pure ternary at full model dim, balanced_ternary init, normalize_projection sqrt_input_dim, trainable_bias, 340,169,484 params, final 1.3580 at 4k) with ONE change: lut_hyperplane_init balanced_ternary -> near_zero_ternary. Everything else identical -- normalize_projection 'sqrt_input_dim' (divisor sqrt(384) ~= 19.5959), trainable_bias true, TernaryHyperplaneMultiHeadLUT, per-table trainable T init 0.5, nonzero_penalty_weight 0.0 (OFF), pure topology (no compress/decompress, full 384-dim input, 384-dim cells, shared-input/summed-heads), n_heads 4, nap 8, tph 128 (512 tables per slot, 6 slots), untied head, forward_mode hard, depth 6 / n_embd 384 / n_head 6 / seq 512, lr 3e-4, wd 0.1, seed 1, device_batch 12 / grad_accum 4 (24,576 tok/step), 4,000 steps on the SAME held 16,000-step LR schedule (warmup 1,600, cosine over 16,000, stop at 4,000), and the SAME ternary_drift.csv instrumentation including the bias columns. Params are IDENTICAL to exp_g_0033 -- only the init VALUES differ, no shapes.
_mem_note: device_batch_size 12 / grad_accum 4 inherited unchanged from exp_g_0029 (effective batch 24,576 tokens). Memory should track exp_g_0029's 14.87 GiB closely -- the ternary path adds one tanh and one sign over the hyperplane weights and nothing on the token axis -- but it is re-verified before launch with a smoke that mirrors a REAL training step: the full grad_accum=4 micro-batch loop on real data plus a real evaluate_bpb, not single micro-batches, which is the trap that let exp_g_0028 pass a smoke and then OOM before step 1. Escalation ladder if it OOMs: expandable_segments first, then device_batch 12 -> 6 with grad_accum 4 -> 8 to preserve the effective batch. Whatever the smoke passes in is the environment the run launches in.
_ternary_note: lut_ternary_temp_init 0.5 is load-bearing, not cosmetic. The dead zone has a closed form: q = 0 exactly when |w| <= 2T*atanh(1/2) = T*ln3 ~= 1.0986*T, so T IS the zero-band width in weight units. At T=0.5 the band is 0.5493, and with hyperplane_init=anchor_pairs the weights are already exactly {-1, 0, +1}: every +-1 survives (1 > 0.5493) and every 0 stays 0. The ternary routing therefore reduces EXACTLY to anchor-pair routing at step 0, matching exp_g_0029's clean start, and the two runs begin from the same selection function. T=1.0 would put the band at 1.0986 > 1 and quantize the whole routing to zeros before training began; the class warns on that and local_ternary_ffn.py escalates it to a hard error. Verified at construction: 2.00 nonzeros per hyperplane, i.e. one +1 and one -1, exactly anchor pairs.
_param_note: Param count is essentially exp_g_0029's: the ternary class keeps the SAME shadow hyperplane_weight [n_tables, nap, 384] as a trainable Parameter during training. Two small differences, both mechanical: it DROPS the bias (hyperplane_bias becomes a frozen all-zero buffer, not a Parameter: -24,576) and ADDS one log_ternary_temp per table (6 x [512,1,1]: +3,072). Net -21,504, i.e. -0.006%. The parameter SAVING from ternarization is a deployment-time property -- after training, bake q to 2 bits per entry and the float weights are never needed again.
_init_note: NEAR-ZERO (DEGENERATE) INIT. Draws w ~ N(0, sigma^2) with sigma chosen so ~99.9% of components land inside the dead zone and quantize to q = 0, using the same derivation as balanced_ternary -- sigma = T*ln3 / Phi^-1((1+f)/2) with f = 0.999 instead of 1/3, giving sigma = 0.166936 at T = 0.5 (band 0.5493). MEASURED at the real shape: +1 0.000476, 0 0.998999, -1 0.000526; 0.3845 non-zeros per hyperplane. The point is to watch how fast the routing GROWS structure from a nearly degenerate start, so the zero->nonzero column of ternary_drift.csv and frac_zero falling over time are the quantities of interest. Two things worth knowing about this start, both measured rather than assumed: only 32.4% of the 4,096 hyperplanes have ANY non-zero component (the other 67.6% produce a constant bit regardless of input), and 96.5% of the 512 tables still have at least one bit that varies with the input -- so the model is heavily degenerate but not totally inert, and the all-zero-routing guard correctly does not fire. Note the contrast with anchor_pairs, which has a similar frac_zero (0.9948) but for the opposite reason: its 2 non-zeros per hyperplane sit at |w| = 1, maximally FAR from the boundary and hence frozen, whereas near_zero's few non-zeros sit close to it.
_bias_note: THE CHANGE: each hyperplane gets one trainable scalar b, shape [n_tables, nap] = [512, 8] per slot, so the routing DECISION becomes <q, x> + b > 0 instead of <q, x> > 0 -- the dead zone can sit off-centre on that hyperplane's own projection axis rather than being pinned symmetric about zero. b is zeroed at construction, so this run starts from EXACTLY the function exp_g_0032 starts from and diverges only as b learns. IMPORTANT distinction: b cannot change q. q = ternary(stanh(w, T)) depends on the weights alone; what b moves is which row a table selects. Unlike the shadow weights, b is RETAINED at deployment as the comparison threshold -- inference stays multiplication-free (adds/subtracts, then one compare against -b instead of against 0). Param delta vs exp_g_0032: +n_tables*nap*depth = 512*8*6 = +24,576 (+0.007%). The drift CSV gains b_min / b_mean / b_max / b_absmean / b_frac_nonzero so we can see whether b actually moves -- it starts at exactly 0 everywhere, so any b_absmean > 0 is the signal.
_normalization_note: WHY: exp_g_0032 diverged badly (behind at 0/8 aligned evals, gap growing monotonically from +0.032 to +0.353 by step 1,600). The balanced init gives ~256 non-zeros per hyperplane instead of anchor_pairs' 2, and <q,x> is a sum of +-1-weighted terms, so its std grows like sqrt(non-zeros): measured 16.04 on the real model, i.e. score/T = 32.1 against the soft_score temperature of 0.5. The surrogate was saturated. DIVISOR = sqrt(input_dim) = sqrt(384) ~= 19.5959. This is the matching correction, since the projection scale grows like the square root of the term count. A first pass used input_dim itself and OVER-corrected: it takes score/T to ~0.08, trading a saturated surrogate for a nearly flat one. Measured at init on the real model: normalized std ~0.818, score/T ~1.64 -- the range the soft-score machinery is actually shaped for. IMPLEMENTATION: the divisor is applied by scaling q, not by editing HyperplaneMultiHeadLUT -- the inherited autograd Functions compute <w,x> + b, so passing q/D yields exactly <q,x>/D + b, which is also why the bias correctly lives in the normalized space. NOTE the hard routing at b=0 is UNCHANGED by the divisor (sign is scale-invariant); what it changes is the temperature-scaled soft/gradient path, and where the threshold sits once b is non-zero. The realized std and score/T are printed at startup, so the choice is judged from data rather than assumed.
